old_route_audit: The cross-fan moment inequalities are correct but saturate at the 3/5 exponent. The initial O(t^4) spherical-polynomial count is correct but superseded and has no novelty claim.
new_result: For two reflection planes, either their product is a rotation of order at most 2t+1 or n <= (e_pi+e_sigma+1)(t+1). Under (2E+1)(t+1)<n, KKPR Theorem 1.2 plus a sharp projective-circle gap argument gives the uniform bound |R_E|<=max(15,2t+2), improving the preliminary O(t^2) count to O(t); equality forces cyclic-coset directions and is attained by planar regular odd polygons in R^3.
additional_result: For three planes in the common-direction branch, their triple reflection is a pure reflection iff the planes share one affine axis; otherwise its square is a nonzero translation. Consequently, under (6E+1)(t+1)<n the entire common-direction subfamily shares one axis. Also, a product rotation of order m has at least n-(e_pi+e_sigma)(m-1) points in complete orbits.
external_input: Kedlaya-Kolpakov-Poonen-Rubinstein, Space vectors forming rational angles, arXiv:2011.14232, Theorem 1.2.
remaining_gap: The extreme small-defect layer is now O(t) and stably coaxial, but no argument connects this near-dihedral structure to the medium-defect reflection energy that controls the 3/5 critical spectrum.
publication_potential: medium-high as a new structural stability theorem or core lemma; not a Q2 main theorem without an exponent gain or broader application
